input.question: How do the same programs run on different operating systems?
input.ground_truth: There are development languages that are cross platform. This is one way this can be accomplished. The same code base will run in various environments (Linux/BSD/Windows) and then OS specific code can be ran inside the software that is called based on what environment the code detects. Also, a second way would be runtime emulation such as WINE, but I don't think that is what you are referring to

Question: How do the same programs run on different operating systems?

Okay! Imagine you have a toy car. You can play with your toy car on the floor at home, or you can take it to the park, or even to grandma’s house. The toy car is the same, but the places you play with it are different.

Now, think of the toy car as a computer program, and the places you play with it (home, park, grandma’s house) as different operating systems (like Windows, Mac, or Linux).

The program is written in a special way so it can play nicely on all these different places. Sometimes, it uses a magic helper (like a “virtual machine” or “interpreter”) that understands how to talk to each different operating system. This way, the same program can run on many different computers, just like your toy car can be played with anywhere!
